title: Unemployment Benefit Claims Waiting Week Rule
content:
On Unemployment Benefit Claims, the first otherwise-payable weeks of a benefit year, up to the program's waiting week count, are served as unpaid waiting weeks.

## The rule the desk applies

- A waiting week is recorded only for a week that would otherwise have been paid in full or in part; a week not certified timely or with good cause, a week with excess earnings or full-time hours, or a week not payable for any other reason does not serve the waiting week.
- A waiting week is recorded only while the number of waiting-week entries on the claim is below the program's waiting week count for the claim.
- No weekly payment is issued on a claim whose program requires a waiting week until the waiting week has been served, and a waiting week is never paid later.
- Programs with a waiting week count of zero pay from the first payable week; an Extended Benefits or Trade Readjustment Allowances claim never serves a waiting week because its parent claim already did.

## Reading the records

The count compared with the program's waiting week count is the number of waiting-week entries on the claim's payment history.

| Waiting-week entries on the claim, against a waiting week count of one | A further waiting week | A weekly payment for a later payable week |
|---|---|---|
| None | Recorded for the first otherwise-payable week | Not issued until the waiting week has been served |
| One | Not recorded | Not barred by the waiting week |

### Hypothetical sequence

On a hypothetical Regular State Unemployment Insurance claim, the first certified week was certified late without good cause and the second week is otherwise payable: the first week does not serve, and the second week is the waiting week, unpaid and never paid later.
